correctness.rationale: For a partial identity e_S, direct comparison of partial-map domains proves that a commuting f preserves S and its complement, giving an exact centralizer product R_k R_{n-k}. The identity R_m=m! L_m(-1) and generating-series convolution yield both finite probabilities without approximation. Perron negative-argument Laguerre asymptotics for alpha=0,1 have correct exponential and polynomial prefactors; substituting (alpha,x)=(0,1),(1,2) derives the stated sharp rare-event probability. The concavity expansion of 2sqrt(k)+2sqrt(n-k) at k=n/2 on n^(3/4) scale yields the normalized Gaussian local density. Summing on bounded intervals and using mass one proves weak convergence and tightness. Standalone independent composition enumeration checks n=0..4, independent integer recurrence and numerical constants pass. Numerical checks alone are not proof.

originality.rationale: A 2012 primary paper on exactly the same monoid already implies the finite centralizer factorization; the claim explicitly excludes it and excludes the standard Laguerre asymptotic. The new object is the joint limiting phenomenon for a random idempotent paired with a random partial bijection: sharp probability prefactor, n^(3/4) Gaussian conditional rank scale and local density. Material from the 2012 article, available later abstracts, own accessible claim comparisons and multiple relevant research-record searches did not identify the same asymptotic proposition or a stronger theorem entailing it. The 2020 centralizer full text was not accessible and historical uniqueness cannot be certified.

value.rationale: The idempotent support rank and commutation are canonical features of the symmetric inverse monoid. The result gives a quantitatively sharp probability of a natural rare relation, plus a full conditional local Gaussian law exhibiting a nonstandard fluctuation scale n^(3/4) compared with the unconditioned binomial sqrt(n) scale. This is a meaningful all-dimensional relationship between algebraic commutation and stochastic rank; it is not motivated solely by a finite table or arbitrary parameter restriction. It does not assert a general unrestricted commuting-pair limit.
